summary: Tim Berners-Lee's system of linked pages, built at CERN to share physics papers. CERN made it royalty-free in 1993, which let it spread to everyone, and it became how most people use the internet.

image.alt: Tim Berners-Lee’s NeXT computer, the first web server, at CERN

events.note: Tim Berners-Lee submits his proposal for an information system to CERN.

events.label: First site
events.note: By the end of 1990 the first browser and web server run at CERN.
The project is announced publicly and opened to everyone.

events.label: Royalty-free
events.note: CERN puts the Web’s software in the public domain.

events.label: W3C
events.note: Berners-Lee founds the World Wide Web Consortium.

sources.title: CERN: The birth of the Web
